:::{#thm-centered-data-rank}
#### A centered data matrix has rank at most $n - 1$

Let $\mX$ be an $n \times p$ matrix with rows $\tp{\vecf{x}_1}, \ldots, \tp{\vecf{x}_n}$,
let $\bar{\vecf{x}} = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n \vecf{x}_i$ be the mean of the rows,
and let $\mX_c = \mX - \v1\,\tp{\bar{\vecf{x}}}$ be the matrix whose row $i$ is $\tp{(\vecf{x}_i - \bar{\vecf{x}})}$,
where $\v1$ is the ones vector of length $n$ (@def-ones-vector).
Then $\operatorname{rank}(\mX_c) \le n - 1$.

:::

::: proof

The entries of each column of $\mX_c$ sum to zero:

$$
\ba
\tp{\v1}\mX_c
&= \tp{\v1}\mX - \paren{\tp{\v1}\v1}\tp{\bar{\vecf{x}}}
&& \text{(@thm-matmul-distrib)}
\\
&= \sum_{i=1}^n \tp{\vecf{x}_i} - n\,\tp{\bar{\vecf{x}}}
&& \text{(} \tp{\v1}\v1 = n \text{)}
\\
&= n\,\tp{\bar{\vecf{x}}} - n\,\tp{\bar{\vecf{x}}}
&& \text{(definition of } \bar{\vecf{x}} \text{)}
\\
&= \tp{\vzero_p}.
\ea
$$

Transposing, $\tp{\mX_c}\v1 = \vzero_p$.
The ones vector is nonzero, so it is in the null space of the $p \times n$ matrix $\tp{\mX_c}$,
and $\operatorname{nullity}(\tp{\mX_c}) \ge 1$.
By @thm-rank-nullity, applied to the $n$ columns of $\tp{\mX_c}$,

$$
\ba
\operatorname{rank}(\mX_c)
&= \operatorname{rank}(\tp{\mX_c})
&& \text{(@thm-rank-transpose)}
\\
&= n - \operatorname{nullity}(\tp{\mX_c})
&& \text{(@thm-rank-nullity)}
\\
&\le n - 1.
&& \text{(} \operatorname{nullity}(\tp{\mX_c}) \ge 1 \text{)}
\ea
$$

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-centered-data-rank}
#### Two points in three dimensions

$\mX = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 3 & 2 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$ has $\bar{\vecf{x}} = (2, 2, 2)$, so

$$
\mX_c = \begin{bmatrix} -1 & 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & -1 \end{bmatrix}.
$$

The second row is $-1$ times the first, so $\operatorname{rank}(\mX_c) = 1 = n - 1$,
and the column sums are zero: $\tp{\v1}\mX_c = \tp{\vzero_3}$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#cor-sample-covariance-singular}
#### A sample covariance matrix from $n \le p$ points is singular

With $\mX_c$ as in @thm-centered-data-rank, the sample covariance matrix

$$
\matr{S} = \frac{1}{n - 1}\,\tp{\mX_c}\mX_c
$$

is $p \times p$ with $\operatorname{rank}(\matr{S}) \le n - 1$.
So if $n \le p$, then $\matr{S}$ is not invertible.

:::

::: proof

$$
\ba
\operatorname{rank}(\matr{S})
&= \operatorname{rank}(\tp{\mX_c}\mX_c)
&& \text{(multiplying by } \tfrac{1}{n-1} \ne 0 \text{ does not change the rank)}
\\
&= \operatorname{rank}(\mX_c)
&& \text{(@thm-rank-transpose)}
\\
&\le n - 1.
&& \text{(@thm-centered-data-rank)}
\ea
$$

If $n \le p$, then $\operatorname{rank}(\matr{S}) \le n - 1 < p$,
so $\matr{S}$ does not have full column rank,
and it is not invertible by @thm-invertible-rank.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-sample-covariance-singular}
#### As many points as dimensions

The $n = 3$ points $(1, 0, 0)$, $(0, 1, 0)$ and $(0, 0, 1)$ in $p = 3$ dimensions have $\bar{\vecf{x}} = \frac{1}{3}(1, 1, 1)$, so

$$
\mX_c = \matr{I}_3 - \tfrac{1}{3}\,\v1\tp{\v1},
\qquad
\matr{S} = \tfrac{1}{2}\,\mX_c
= \tfrac{1}{6}\begin{bmatrix} 2 & -1 & -1 \\ -1 & 2 & -1 \\ -1 & -1 & 2 \end{bmatrix},
$$

using $\tp{\mX_c}\mX_c = \mX_c$ (the centering matrix is a symmetric projection).
Then $\matr{S}\,\v1 = \vzero_3$ and $\operatorname{rank}(\matr{S}) = 2 = n - 1 < 3$.
With one more point than dimensions ($n = p + 1$), the rank bound allows $\matr{S}$ to have full rank $p$.

:::
